what_happened: The job added an urgent priority level and a priority-record command that plan uses. It was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier gave one major finding. In docs/decisions.md (lines 3005-3053), the new entry D122 was inserted inside D121. D121 lost its Provenance bullet, and D122 ended with D121's provenance. No acceptance criteria and no failed checks are listed in the event, so the stored fields show only this docs edit defect. The code work is not reported as faulty.
cause: Nothing in code checks the structure of the append-only decisions log after an edit. The producer inserted a new entry by position in a long file. Nothing verifies that each entry keeps its own fields, such as the Provenance bullet, or that new entries are only appended after the last one. Only the verifier's reading of the diff at the final verdict catches the damaged adjacent entry, and there rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show how the edit was made.
prevention: Add a code check that runs before handover and again in the repo tests. It parses docs/decisions.md into entries and requires three things. (1) Each entry has the required fields, including a Provenance bullet. (2) Entry ids are unique and strictly ascending. (3) Against the base version, every existing entry is byte-identical and the only change is entries appended at the end. An insertion inside an existing entry then fails the check, and the producer sees the failure and fixes it before the verifier does.
proposed_request: Fix docs/decisions.md so D121 and D122 are each whole again. D121 must have its own Provenance bullet back, and D122 must have the provenance that belongs to it. Append D122 after D121 rather than inside it. Then add a repo test that parses docs/decisions.md into entries and checks three things. Every entry has all required fields, including Provenance. Ids are unique and ascending. Against the base commit, existing entries are unchanged and the only additions are entries appended at the end. Acceptance: the test fails on the current broken file and passes after the fix. Changes are limited to docs/decisions.md and the new test. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` pass, and the evidence cites the commands actually run.
